newsitem.title: GERMANY: German equities end on a high, lifted by dollar.
newsitem.headline: German equities end on a high, lifted by dollar.

text.p: Bulls ran rampant in electronic share trade in Frankfurt on Friday afternoon as the dollar penetrated the 1.67-mark threshold and the Dow Jones Industrial index opened sharply higher to underpin lively IBIS DAX trade.
The IBIS DAX index of electronic trade in 30 German blue-chips continued its record-breaking run to end the day at an all-time closing high of 3,161.36 points, up 36.58 points or 1.17 points.
Earlier, the DAX index, which gauges bourse trade, also ended on a record high at 3,138.01 points, up 33.87 points or 1.09 percent.
Dealers said there were no bearish signs in sight to stymie the seemingly unstoppable advance of the German share market at the moment.
"Just look at the dollar - we've been through 1.67 marks and are now above that, U.S. non-farm payroll data were good and Wall Street is up -- a classic bull market," said one trader.
"It could be that everything looks a little bit exaggerated right now and it won't look so rosy on Monday morning. But we are still in liquidity markets, markets that want to go up," said the trader.
"While all the ingredients are there to go higher, we have to go higher," said the trader.

Dealers said that if the Dow Jones Industrial index on Wall Street continues its rally, if the dollar stays around current levels and if the G7 meeting of finance ministers in Berlin at the weekend does not produce any unexpected findings, the bull run could continue next week.

One possible downside for the market is Germany's pre-Lent Fasching holiday. The annual regional holiday, which took off in earnest on Thursday, has a greater impact in northern Germany and does not affect Frankfurt until Tuesday when markets close for the afternoon.
Dealers said that volumes might be muted, but that in its current position there was no real reason to suspect any major impact on the trend and for volumes to contract significantly.

Volume leader in afternoon trade was electronics group Siemens AG which started its rise after breaking an important technical barrier at 81 marks, and continued its rise boosted by a mixture of positive fundamental factors and an element of market rumour.
Market speculation about a possible restructuring by Siemens, which traders said could be announced next week, drove the share higher on Thursday and continued on Friday morning.

Siemens ended the day at 86.08 marks, up 79 pfennigs, off earlier highs of 86.34 marks. The share's rise on Friday started with news it had won an order to supply equipment for the German D2 mobile phone system operated by the German phone company Mannesmann Mobilfunk.
Bayerische Vereinsbank and Dresdner Bank also raised their rating and earnings outlook respectively for Siemens shares, which helped lift the share price.
"We are seeing a lot of sector rotation at the moment -- banks, chemicals -- today it's second-liners," said a trader.

The chemical sector saw considerable volumes, with the high dollar, and BASF AG ended up 1.13 marks at 62.48 marks, Bayer AG up 49 pfennigs at 65.80 marks and Hoechst AG up 51 pfennigs at 72.80 marks.
Veba AG ended up 17 pfennigs at 92.12 marks, off earlier highs, after C&W withdrew from a telecoms alliance and a seperate telecoms deal with RWE received cartel office approval.
